## Headline

A mid-month check-in, written on the 19th with March about three-fifths elapsed. Spending stands at $4,923.98 across fifty-four entries so far — on the heavy side for a part-month, and two stories explain it: the tech refresh and the Niagara client trip.

## Key findings

Technology is the biggest discretionary line at $495.43 — the Best Buy monitor run on the 9th ($185.59) and the Apple Store visit on the 17th ($309.84) that had been deferred since the new-year sales. Travel shows the Enterprise Rent-A-Car pickup on the 13th ($147.85) for the overnight client visit to Niagara; the two Petro-Canada stops around it are the first gasoline on the cards in the entire visible year — Mira does not own a car, so fuel only appears when a rental does.

## Category deep dives

Groceries are already at $571.88 across seven runs, anchored by a $178.41 Loblaws Queen West shop on the 7th — the biggest basket of the winter. Dining sits at $395.67 across sixteen entries, halfway between January's quiet and December's bustle. The two LCBO stops ($121.07) both fell on the trip-adjacent weekend.

## Alerts

The dining pace is running ahead of where the envelope expects it at this point in the month — not dramatically, but the creep has been visible since February's reentry weekend.

## Easy notes

Rent posted at $2,150 on the 1st. Toronto Hydro came in at $92.13, continuing its slow descent from the January peak. Subscriptions held at $55.72. The Northwind retainer landed on schedule on the 15th.

## Outlook

Twelve days remain. The month-end sweep on the 28th will show whether the tech refresh squeezed the TFSA contribution; on current pace the month lands close to even, and April opens with the cabin weekend already paid for.
